EINSTIEN GARRY R. TAGHOY City Legal Officer Digos City, Davao Del Sur Dear Atty. Einstien Garry R. Taghoy: 2010 This Office was in receipt of a Memorandum from Regional Director (RD) Quirino M. Libunao of DILG Regional Office No. XI, Davao City, in response to your query which was earlier referred to the said office for appropriate action. The query centers on the propriety of your act as City Legal Officer when you notarized a contract between the winning bidder and the City Government of Digos when at the same time, you occupy a as represented by the City Mayor, concurrent position as Chairperson of the Bid and Awards Committee (BAC) who approved the contract of the same winning bidder. Attached to the said Memorandum is the position maintained by our Regional Office in Davao City, signed by RD Libunao himself, and in gist, we quote the pertinent portion theréof: "The law is clear that public officials and employees are generally prohibited from engaging in the private practice of their profession unless authorized by the Constitution or law. As opined by the Supreme Court, the only exceptions are as follows: first, the private practice is authorized by the Constitution or the law; and second, the practice will not conflict, or tend to conflict, with his or her official functions. xxx We are of the considered view that there is a conflict or tendency to conflict with official function of the Legal Officer as BAC Chair if such act of notarization is allowed. It bears to stress that the functions of BAC are so encompassing on procurement activities of the LGU.xxx. " (emphasis and underscoring supplied) We are of the opinion that the position as explained by RD I-ibunao is in order. While the documents under review by this Office did not mention of any issue as to the existence or absence of your authority to practice your profession as a lawyer, the same shall be discussed as an integral part of this Office's additional legal authorities on the matter.

On the matter of engaging in notarial practice without the written authority from the Department Head, we cite the case of Abella vs Atty. Cruzabra, A.C. No. 5688, 04 June 2009 wherein said respondent was reprimanded with stern warning by the Supreme Court for engaging in notarial practice without authority from the Department Secretary: "Memorandum Circular No. 17 of the Executive Department alloros government employees to engage directly in the private practice of Illeir profession provided [here is a toritten perjnission fronl Ihe Depnrtntent Ilead. It provides: Tile anthorily to grant perillission Io any official or employee shall be granted by [he head of the ministry or agency in accordance rvilll Section 12, Rule XVIII of the Revised Civil Service Rules, collicll provides: "Sec. 12. No officer or entployee shall engage directly in any private business, vocation, or profession or be connected cpitll any connnercinl, credit, agricultural, or industrial undertaking 71'it11011t a written permission from the head of Department; xxx. " (emplmsis supplied) Thus, it is emphasized by this Office that your notarial practice must have a prior written authorization from the City Mayor of Digos, Davao who has control and supervision over your position. Absent such authority, then the notarial act subject of this review is deemed improper and a prohibitive act. Assuming arguendo that you have a standing authority to practice your profession, the act of notarizing the contract which you approved as Chairperson of the BAC of Digos City was contrary to the norms of conduct expected of public officials. Republic Act No. 6713, otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, commitment to public interest and professionalism : "Section 4.
